image.alt: Siri and his companions examine a large teleportation circle beneath the Great Shield Cathedral of Keinra with Sister Mari

paragraphs: 兩天的時間，在瑪莉修女的協助下，冒險者們依然沒有找到魔法陣的位置。
「我不懂⋯⋯」瑪莉修女露出了少見的困擾的神情。「大教堂的地下空間就這麼大，我們都繞了好幾回了，怎麼可能找不到？」
看著喜力依循自己的記憶畫出的地圖，冒險者們確實把所有可見的空間都繞過一遍了。地下一層、地下兩層，沒有任何繼續向下通的入口，依照羅賓遜主教的了解，大教堂也就兩層地下空間，要是有地下三層的話，那也完全突破他的認知了。
「我們是不是以前也有遇過類似的事情啊？」YHWH 靠著地下二樓的牆壁喃喃自語著。「當時在麥克嵩的日出酒館，那個衛兵說他住在酒館的二樓，但我們怎麼都找不到通往二樓的地方。我說的沒錯吧，米多莉？」此時，YHWH 的手上已冒出微微的火光。
「YHWH 你先等一下。」米多莉抿著嘴唇。「這裡是津菈教堂，不是你可以亂燒的地方。」
「好吧。」YHWH 的臉色顯然有些失落，但此刻的波卻沒有露出一貫的鄙視眼神---他更像專注著該怎麼解決問題，不過是用不太聰明的作法：他到處踏著地板，用手肘敲牆壁，有時甚至用腳踢了踢。當然，教堂穩固的結構沒有任何影響。
「酷爆說他什麼奇怪的味道都沒有聞到。」薩梅爾掏出給酷爆準備的食物，獎賞他這幾個小時認真的搜索。「會不會我們漏掉什麼暗門之類的啊？」
「所有暗門可能存在的地方我都摸過一遍了，也都沒感受到異樣的魔法。」喜利十分肯定的說道。「連鎖頭都沒有的話，我的開鎖工具也無『鎖』發揮。」
「如果那隻『狐狸』可以變成貓的話，是不是我們應該用動物的角度去思考才對啊？」薩梅爾摸著正在大口啃食的酷爆的頭。「酷爆，又是你登場的機會了！」
「那看起來沒我的是，還是我先回樓上客房休息？」YHWH 站起了身，已經準備上樓了。「酷爆，靠你囉！」話還沒說完，YHWH 就看見波蹲在地上四腳爬行。「你們看，波平常嫌棄我覺得我很怪，那現在是誰在地上爬？」
「那不然，YHWH 你先上去休息，我們其他人繼續找。」米多莉嚴肅地看了看 YHWH。「我們找到了再告訴你。」
「那就掰掰囉。」YHWH 踏著輕盈的步伐朝著樓上走去。
說時遲那時快，龍恩已一拳一拳揮向塔爾莫的臉。「你、怎麼、會、在、這裡？」
「師弟啊師弟，看來你也成長不少呢，我真是感到欣慰。」塔爾莫的鼻子似乎歪了，卻仍微笑著，也不必開龍恩的拳頭。「見到你我很開心呢。」
「你、還沒、回答、我、問題！」龍恩沒停下拳頭。他想過再打下去，他的師兄會不會就這樣沒命，但⋯⋯好像也沒什麼關係。
「你的手，」塔爾莫用他的手嘗試接住龍恩那隻變異的手。「用得還習慣嗎？」
「這隻嗎？」龍恩頓了下來。「這隻也不知道怎麼來的，蠻酷的。雖然不是金屬手臂，但好像比金屬還厲害。」
「妖精荒野。」塔爾莫微笑看著龍恩，一手終於找到空檔擦拭他溢血的臉頰。「你大概不記得那個地方了吧？」
「我好像聽我之前的冒險夥伴提過，但我自己是不記得了啦。」龍恩輕輕皺了眉頭。「阿這跟手臂有什麼關係？你又怎麼知道？」
一段熟悉卻又陌生的語句從塔爾莫口中傳出。龍恩似乎有印象自己在哪聽過。
「這是拉索斯語。」塔爾莫輕聲說著。「意思是『本該屬於你的東西，終究會回到你身邊』。那是我在妖精荒野的中心樹前，對你說的話。也許你認不得、聽不懂，甚至不記得了，但看見你把那隻手臂接上，我的目標就達成了。」
「所以這隻手是你給我的？」龍恩歪著頭，看向點著頭的塔爾莫。「為什麼？」
「現在你相信我了吧？我們找個安靜點的地方談吧。」塔爾莫朝旁邊比劃，一個黑色的漩渦逐漸成形。接著塔爾莫緩緩走進漩渦內。龍恩一開始有點猶疑，手微微深入，發現沒什麼痛感，收回來手也還在，秉持著一點好奇心，也就踏入了這漩渦內。
尖頂寺住持的廳堂內，罕見地在午夜打起了光。
「方丈大師！我們---」
「我知道。」年邁的僧人盤腿靜坐著。他的雙眼闔上，僅舉起一隻手，衝入廳堂內的僧人們都停了下來。「那你們有什麼想法？尚恩，你比較了解他，對吧？」
一名青年僧人向前踏了一步，恭敬的雙手向住持作揖。「師父，請容我向您說明---」
「這種危急時刻，禮儀什麼的就別管了，解決問題要緊。」住持睜開了雙眼。「你們都進來吧，鞋子也不用脫了，這裡沒有外人。我們圍著茶桌好好討論。巴多、里奧波，你們在門口站崗，有任何風吹草動就回報。」
「師父，我和其他師兄想到了兩個方法，可以把那叛徒困在這裡，以及把問題解決。」尚恩還是改不掉對著住持低頭說話的習慣。「我之前曾在麥克嵩參與比武大會，那時基於好奇，有打探了龍恩在那邊的狀況。」
「繼續說。」住持貌似悠閒的泡起了茶，從抽屜拿出了五個陶瓷的樸素茶杯。
「龍恩在那裡似乎有了十分在意的一個女人，一名貴族女子，名叫蘿琳・休斯。也許她能作為一個好用的棋子。」
「然後呢？」住持有耐心地等著茶壺煮開。水溫不夠燙，茶的風味不夠香濃。
「如果師父允許⋯⋯我們可以架起魔法屏障，對外界只保留大門的唯一入口，加倍守衛的弟兄。然後派一支小隊去麥克嵩與休斯女士交涉，看能否說服她來尖頂寺坐鎮。」
「就這麼辦。」沒有一秒多想，住持就同意了。「尚恩，就你帶隊去吧，史坦、依曼紐、馮里，你們一起去，也把巴多和里奧波一起帶去。除了你們之外，其他人都還不知道吧？」住持一邊說著，一邊把茶杯收到剩下一個。「魔法屏障我來負責，有需要也還有眾長老可以輔助我。你們出發吧，低調點。」
雖然對妖精荒野發生的事搞不清楚，但師兄說的話，似乎自成一套道理。隆恩花了幾天反覆思索，也沒找到什麼破綻。塔爾莫的鼻子還綁著繃帶，說不定鼻梁這一歪，就歪一輩子了，但塔爾莫似乎不在意。
依照塔爾莫的說法，在他離開尖頂寺後幾年的時間，他曾過得風光。但在意氣風發之時，得罪了一些不該得罪的派系，導致自己得像過街老鼠般在不同寺院間流竄。最終還是與尖頂寺有關的拉索斯教會收留了他，讓他好好避風頭。
那間名為「灰祠」的小教堂，偏僻而落寞，但裡面卻有著不得了的東西。一隻被裡頭神父和修女謹慎保護的奇怪手臂。在那裡待一段時間後，塔爾莫也終於被分配單獨看守這奇怪的東西。好奇心不只會殺死貓，還會讓自己做些瘋狂事。塔爾莫揮劍，砍斷了自己的手，卻怎麼也接不上這隻乾枯的手臂---說實在，也不是誰教他這麼作，就是種⋯⋯原始的衝動。儘管如此，他還是清楚知道這是非凡之物，因此他還是趁夜摸走了這手臂，成為了逃犯。
身為半妖精，有著妖精血統的塔爾莫想到了妖精荒野這個遺世之處，正適合作為他的逃亡之地。他帶著手臂，低調地來到了妖精荒野，長時間待在荒野之中，終於找到機會混入大帳篷內。而他沒想到的是，竟然會在這裡看見多年未見的親愛的小師弟。
塔爾莫聽見了小師弟對著中心樹喃喃自語，彷彿命中註定般地央求著金屬手臂。這一刻，他徹底相信了：這世界如果有什麼「被選中的人」，那人肯定不是他自己。至少龍恩比他更像這樣的身份。
以前，是年幼的龍恩懵懵懂懂地跟著他；現在，他已下定決心，要助龍恩一臂之力---不過這也是因為他只剩下一隻手臂。只不過，塔爾莫回到物質世界的這段路，走得比他預期慢了好幾年的時間。說實在，他也不記得為什麼了。在妖精荒野的記憶，像是被篩選過一樣，有些事情，再怎麼想，塔爾莫也想不起來。
YHWH 從香甜的夢中醒來。這一晚特別舒服，整個房間只有他一人，其他夥伴似乎都還沒回來。說實在，好像應該去看一下比較好。他站起身，伸了個懶腰，腰有些痠疼，大概是睡姿不太正確吧。年紀也到了。
正要走向門口，客房的房門就被急促地推開。喜利飛快的身影出現在 YHWH 眼前。
「他們找到了。」喜利急促地說著。「酷爆、酷爆真的找到了。」
二十分鐘後，YHWH 和喜利拎著大夥兒的行李，出現在了聖津菈大教堂的地下二樓。他們望向擁擠的掃具間，裡面光是波和薩梅爾就擠滿了。波正在拿著她的劍朝著某個角落用力地刺，薩梅爾則抱著酷爆愣著看。
「掃具間的水桶後面有個比較大的磚頭有些鬆動。酷爆鑽了進去，發現地下有個不小的空間。」米多莉彷彿也還沒相信這件事，恍恍地和 YHWH 解釋。「現在波再把它鑿開，我們才進得去。」
「這時候就交給我吧！」YHWH 得意的笑了笑，捲起袖子。
「欸不是，這是磚頭，不是木頭啊！」喜利趕緊拉住 YHWH 的衣角。「而且要是裡面燒了，搞不好就傳送不了了！」
「搞定！」波站了起身，差點撞到正走近的 YHWH。她皺了皺眉，然後率先爬了下去。YHWH 見狀，也跟著爬進了鑿開的洞口，然後還是點起了火，照亮了這個空間。「謝謝你，YHWH。」
眾人落地後，看清楚了地面的法陣。由不明粉末圍起的完整圓圈，繞著如圖示般密密麻麻的文字。六顆奇形怪狀的石頭，以相同的距離，放置在圓周上。
「我看過這種東西。」喜利十分肯定地說道。「但我不知道怎麼用。」
「喔，這個我也看過。」YHWH 喜孜孜地說著。「以前在大學城的時候有看過別人用，但我也只是看過而已。」
此時，波已站在圓圈內其中兩顆石頭中間。「你們站進來吧，每個人站一個空隙。」
「你怎麼知道該怎麼做？」YHWH 訝異地看著波。
「這是很基礎的拉索斯語。上面寫得很清楚。」波不帶特別情緒地說著，可以看出她已經十分疲憊了。「我們五個，酷爆也算一個吧。」然後他轉頭看向瑪莉修女。「瑪莉，妳也要一起來嗎？」
「我⋯⋯我也一起嗎？」瑪莉修女愣了一下。
波點了點頭。「妳也想拯救龍恩吧？」
「你們真的願意讓我跟著一起去嗎？」瑪莉修女看向冒險者們，喃喃自語道。「要的話，我也得先告訴羅賓遜主教一聲。」
Two days had passed, and even with Sister Mari's help, the adventurers still had not found the magic circle.
“I don't understand...” Sister Mari wore a rare look of frustration. “The cathedral's underground chambers are only so big. We've been around them several times. How can we still not have found it?”

Looking at the map Siri had drawn from memory, the adventurers had indeed explored every visible space. The first basement, the second basement—there was no entrance leading any farther down. As far as Bishop Robinson knew, the cathedral had only two underground levels. A third would be entirely beyond his knowledge.

“Haven't we run into something like this before?” YHWH murmured, leaning against the wall of the second basement. “Back at Sunrise tavern in Macksohn, that guard said he lived upstairs, but we couldn't find any way up. Isn't that right, Midori?” A faint flame was already flickering in his hand.
“Hold on, YHWH.” Midori pressed her lips together. “This is a Keinra church. You can't just burn things here.”

“All right.” YHWH looked distinctly disappointed. For once, however, Beau did not give him her usual contemptuous look. She seemed more intent on solving the problem, albeit through methods that were not particularly clever: stamping on the floor, knocking on the walls with her elbow, and occasionally kicking them. Naturally, none of this made any impression on the cathedral's sturdy structure.

“Kubao says he hasn't smelled anything strange.” Samael took out some food he had brought for Kubao, rewarding him for several hours of diligent searching. “Could we have missed a hidden door or something?”

“I've felt every spot where a hidden door could be, and I haven't sensed any unusual magic either,” Siri said with certainty. “Without even a lock, my lockpicks haven't had a chance to unlock their potential.”
“If that ‘Fox’ can turn into a cat, maybe we should be thinking from an animal's point of view?” Samael stroked Kubao's head as the wolf ate heartily. “Kubao, here's your chance to shine again!”

“Then I guess there's nothing for me to do. Maybe I'll head upstairs and rest in the guest room?” YHWH rose, already preparing to leave. “We're counting on you, Kubao!” Before he had finished, he saw Beau drop to all fours. “Look at that! Beau always acts like I'm the weird one. Who's crawling around on the floor now?”
“Why don't you go upstairs and rest, YHWH? The rest of us will keep looking.” Midori gave him a serious look. “We'll let you know when we find it.”
“See you, then.” With a spring in his step, YHWH headed upstairs.
In an instant, Ron was raining punches down on Tar'Mo's face. “What. Are. You. Doing. Here?”
“My dear junior, you've certainly grown. I'm so pleased.” Tar'Mo's nose appeared to have been knocked crooked, yet he kept smiling and made no move to avoid Ron's fists. “It's good to see you.”
“You. Still. Haven't. Answered. Me!” Ron kept punching. He wondered whether another few blows might kill his senior, but... perhaps that would not matter much.
“Your hand.” Tar'Mo reached out, trying to catch Ron's altered hand. “Have you gotten used to it?”
“This one?” Ron paused. “I don't know where it came from, but it's pretty cool. It's not a metal arm, but it seems even better than metal.”
“The Feywild.” Tar'Mo smiled at Ron, finally finding an opening to wipe the blood from his cheek. “You probably don't remember that place, do you?”
“I think my old adventuring companions mentioned it, but I don't remember it myself.” Ron frowned slightly. “What's that got to do with my arm? And how do you know?”
Tar'Mo spoke a phrase that sounded both familiar and strange. Ron had a vague sense that he had heard it somewhere before.

“That was Laxthosian,” Tar'Mo said softly. “It means, ‘What was meant to be yours will find its way back to you in the end.’ That's what I said to you before the central tree in the Feywild. Perhaps you didn't recognize it, understand it, or even remember it. But once I saw you attach that arm, my purpose was fulfilled.”
“So you gave me this hand?” Ron tilted his head, watching Tar'Mo nod. “Why?”

“Do you believe me now? Let's find somewhere quieter to talk.” Tar'Mo gestured to one side, and a black vortex slowly took shape. He stepped into it. Ron hesitated at first. He put his hand a little way inside; it did not hurt, and when he pulled it back, it was still there. With a little curiosity to spur him on, he stepped into the vortex too.
At midnight, lights burned in the abbot's hall at Peak Temple, an unusual sight.
“Master Abbot! We—”

“I know.” The elderly monk sat cross-legged in meditation, eyes closed. He merely raised one hand, and the monks rushing into the hall stopped. “What do you propose? Sean, you know him better than most, don't you?”
A young monk stepped forward and bowed respectfully with his hands clasped. “Master, please allow me to explain—”

“At a time like this, never mind the formalities. Solving the problem comes first.” The abbot opened his eyes. “Come in, all of you. Leave your shoes on; there are no outsiders here. Let's discuss this around the tea table. Bar'Do, Leopold, stand guard at the door. Report anything unusual.”

“Master, the other senior brothers and I have come up with two measures to keep that traitor here and resolve the problem.” Sean could not break his habit of lowering his head when addressing the abbot. “I once competed in the tournament at Macksohn. Out of curiosity, I made some inquiries about Ron while I was there.”
“Go on.” The abbot began preparing tea with apparent leisure, taking five plain ceramic cups from a drawer.
“It seems Ron has a woman there whom he cares for very much. A noblewoman named Roline Hughes. Perhaps she could be a useful pawn.”
“And then?” The abbot waited patiently for the kettle to boil. Unless the water was hot enough, the tea would lack its full aroma.

“If you permit it, Master... we could erect a magical barrier, leaving the main gate as the only way in from outside, and double the brothers on guard. Then we could send a small party to Macksohn to speak with Lady Hughes and see whether she can be persuaded to come and stay at Peak Temple.”

“Do it.” The abbot agreed without a moment's hesitation. “Sean, you will lead the party. Stan, Emmanuel, Lee Feng, go with him, and take Bar'Do and Leopold too. No one besides you knows yet, correct?” As he spoke, he put away all but one of the teacups. “I'll handle the barrier. The elders can assist me if needed. Be on your way, and keep a low profile.”

Though Ron still could not make sense of what had happened in the Feywild, his senior's account seemed internally consistent. He spent several days turning it over in his mind without finding a flaw. Tar'Mo's nose was still bandaged. Perhaps it would stay crooked for the rest of his life, but Tar'Mo did not seem to mind.

According to Tar'Mo, he had enjoyed a few glorious years after leaving Peak Temple. At the height of his success, however, he had offended factions he should never have crossed, forcing him to scurry from monastery to monastery like a hunted rat. Eventually, a Laxthos church with ties to Peak Temple took him in and gave him a place to lie low.

The little chapel, called the Grey Shrine, was remote and forlorn, but it housed something extraordinary: a strange arm, carefully guarded by its priests and nuns. After staying there for some time, Tar'Mo was finally assigned to watch the peculiar thing alone. Curiosity did more than kill cats; it drove people to madness. Tar'Mo swung his sword and cut off his own hand, but no matter what he tried, he could not attach the withered arm. In truth, no one had told him to do it. It was simply a kind of... primal impulse. Even so, he knew it was no ordinary relic. He stole away with the arm one night and became a fugitive.

A half-elf with fey ancestry, Tar'Mo thought of the Feywild, a place apart from the world and an ideal refuge. Taking the arm with him, he slipped quietly into the Feywild. After a long stay in the wilds, he finally found a chance to sneak into the great tent. What he never expected was to find his dear little junior there after so many years.

He heard his junior murmuring to the central tree, pleading for a metal arm as though fate itself had brought him there. In that moment, Tar'Mo became utterly convinced: if anyone in this world was a “chosen one,” it certainly was not him. Ron, at least, fit the role better.

In the old days, a young and bewildered Ron had followed him around. Now Tar'Mo had resolved to lend Ron a hand—though, admittedly, he had only one arm left to lend. His journey back to the Material Realm, however, took several years longer than he had expected. In truth, he could no longer remember why. His memories of the Feywild seemed to have been sifted through. Some things remained beyond his reach, no matter how hard he tried to recall them.

YHWH woke from a sweet dream. The night had been particularly comfortable: he had the room all to himself, and his companions apparently had not come back yet. Really, he ought to check on them. He stood and stretched. His lower back ached a little; perhaps he had slept in an awkward position. He was getting on in years, after all.
Just as he was about to head for the door, it burst open. Siri's swift figure appeared before him.
“They found it,” Siri said breathlessly. “Kubao—Kubao really found it.”

Twenty minutes later, YHWH and Siri arrived in the second basement of the Great Shield Cathedral of Keinra, carrying everyone's luggage. They peered into the crowded cleaning cupboard, where Beau and Samael alone took up nearly all the space. Beau was driving her sword hard into a corner, while Samael stood staring, Kubao in his arms.

“One of the larger bricks behind a bucket in the cleaning cupboard was loose. Kubao squeezed through and found a fairly big space underneath.” Midori explained it to YHWH in a daze, as if she still could not quite believe it herself. “Now Beau's widening the opening so we can get in.”
“Leave this to me!” YHWH grinned proudly and rolled up his sleeves.
“Wait, those are bricks, not wood!” Siri hurriedly caught the hem of YHWH's clothes. “Besides, if you burn what's inside, we might not be able to teleport at all!”

“Done!” Beau stood, nearly colliding with YHWH as he approached. She frowned, then climbed down first. YHWH followed her through the opening and lit a flame after all, illuminating the chamber. “Thank you, YHWH.”

Once everyone was down, they could make out the magic circle on the floor. An unbroken ring of unidentified powder surrounded densely packed writing that resembled diagrams. Six oddly shaped stones were set at equal intervals around the circumference.
“I've seen something like this,” Siri said confidently. “But I don't know how to use it.”
“Oh, I've seen one too,” YHWH said cheerfully. “I saw people use one back in Great Citadel. But I only watched.”
By then, Beau was already standing inside the circle, between two of the stones. “Come in. Each of you stand in one of the gaps.”
“How do you know what to do?” YHWH looked at her in surprise.

“This is very basic Laxthosian. The instructions are quite clear.” Beau's voice carried no particular emotion; she was visibly exhausted. “There are five of us. Kubao counts as one too, I suppose.” Then she turned to Sister Mari. “Mari, are you coming with us?”
“I... you want me to come too?” Sister Mari froze for a moment.
Beau nodded. “You want to save Ron too, don't you?”
“Would you really let me come along?” Sister Mari murmured, looking at the adventurers. “If so, I'll need to let Bishop Robinson know first.”
